author: reek
body: Replay, defeated. Every assertion here is validly signed by the owner -- the attack is not forgery, it is copying an old signature forward in the log to override a newer one. a.codex is retired at t2 and re-added at t3; the old t2 tombstone is then replayed at the end of the log, and must NOT retire the re-added file, because t2 is older than t3. b.codex is retired at t2; its original t1 definition is then replayed at the end of the log, and must NOT resurrect it, because t1 is older than t2. The verified index resolves each path by the signed timestamp, so neither replay lands. A genuinely newer tombstone (t9) still retires a.codex, so removal itself is not broken.
